new.name: EXPLAINS_OBSERVED_ANOMALY
new.definition: The reasoning accounts causally for why a recorded observation produced an unexpected, empty, or puzzling result, naming a concrete mechanism (tool/option semantics, symlink handling, process lifecycle) instead of treating the result as a failure of the underlying goal.

parameters.name: explanation
parameters.description: The agent text that accounts for the puzzling result.

parameters.name: anomalous_observation
parameters.description: The observation whose output was empty, missing, or contrary to expectation.

assertion_conditions: The explanation explicitly refers to a result contained in the observation that deviated from expectation or left a property undetermined.
The explanation identifies a concrete cause for that result (e.g., a command not following symlinks, a shell lacking a numeric conversion function, a non-reaping parent process).
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning merely restates or quotes the observation without a causal account.
The reasoning only proposes the next action and gives no cause for the puzzling result.
The referenced result is not present in the observation (no traceable link between the two nodes).

new.name: REVERIFIES_WITH_ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISM
new.definition: A prior observation left a system property undetermined or contradicted expectation, and the action re-establishes that same property through a different tool, option, or access path rather than repeating the original check.

parameters.name: recheck_action
parameters.description: The action performing the alternative re-verification.

parameters.name: inconclusive_observation
parameters.description: The earlier check whose output was empty, ambiguous, or insufficient to settle the property.

assertion_conditions: The prior observation failed to reveal a property that the agent expected or needed to know.
The action inspects the same system property using a different command, option, or access path than the earlier check.
The differing technique is what makes the property observable.
exclusion_conditions: The action reruns the identical command with identical options, adding no new observability.
The action inspects a different property than the one left undetermined.
The earlier observation was conclusive, so the action is routine verification rather than alternative re-verification.

new.name: RESOLVES_FUNCTIONAL_DOUBT_BY_PROBE
new.definition: The reasoning raises doubt about whether an observed anomaly actually impairs a required capability, a probe action exercises exactly that capability, and the resulting observation demonstrates the capability still works, allowing the anomaly to be dismissed.

parameters.name: doubt_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text expressing uncertainty about whether the anomaly breaks functionality.

parameters.name: probe_action
parameters.description: The action that exercises the capability put in doubt.

parameters.name: probe_result
parameters.description: The observation reporting the outcome of the probe.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning identifies an observed anomaly and questions whether it affects a required capability.
The probe action directly exercises the capability that was questioned.
The probe result shows the capability behaving successfully, providing grounds to treat the anomaly as harmless.
exclusion_conditions: The probe does not target the capability that was questioned.
The probe result is failing, inconclusive, or unrelated to the doubt.
No doubt about functionality is expressed; the probe is ordinary acceptance testing.

new.name: VERIFIES_ENUMERATED_STATE_ITEMS
new.definition: The reasoning itemizes discrete facets of system state to be confirmed, and the action performs a read-only inspection that reads back those same facets in one pass.

parameters.name: inspection_action
parameters.description: The read-only action that reads back the enumerated state facets.

parameters.name: checklist_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text enumerating the specific facets to be confirmed.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning lists multiple discrete facets to confirm (services, listening ports, ownership/permissions, repository refs, configuration contents, HTTP status).
The action issues read-only commands covering those same facets.
The facets checked by the action can be mapped onto the enumerated items.
exclusion_conditions: The action mutates state rather than reading it back.
The action checks facets that were not enumerated, or the reasoning gives only a general goal without itemized facets.
The reasoning enumerates items but the action addresses only one of them.

new.name: PROVISIONS_DISPOSABLE_CREDENTIAL
new.definition: The action creates transient authentication material in a temporary location and installs it into the authentication path solely so that the login or authentication flow can be exercised during testing, without intending it as the end user's credential.

parameters.name: provisioning_action
parameters.description: The action generating and installing the temporary credential.

assertion_conditions: The action generates authentication material (key pair, token) at a temporary path.
The generated material is placed into the authentication path (e.g., an authorized-keys file) so that a test login can succeed.
The material is distinct from the credential the end user is expected to configure.
exclusion_conditions: The action sets up the credential the end user will keep and use.
The action only reads or inspects existing credentials without generating new material.
Generated material is intended for permanent production use rather than a test of the authentication path.

new.name: REPLICATES_DOCUMENTED_USER_COMMANDS
new.definition: The reasoning lays out the exact command sequence the requester is expected to run, and the action executes that sequence verbatim against the configured system in a fresh working location as an acceptance replay.

parameters.name: replay_action
parameters.description: The action executing the documented command sequence.

parameters.name: sequence_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text enumerating the expected command sequence.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning enumerates the specific commands the requester will run, in order.
The action executes those same commands, in the same order, rather than ad-hoc equivalents.
The execution occurs in a clean location so the result reflects the requester's starting conditions.
exclusion_conditions: The action uses substitute commands that only approximate the documented workflow.
The reasoning states general verification goals without listing a concrete command sequence.
The action executes only a fragment of the documented sequence.

new.name: INSTALLS_STARTUP_HOOK
new.definition: The action modifies shell startup configuration so that a previously created helper is invoked automatically on future interactive or login shells, wiring the helper into the session lifecycle.

parameters.name: hook_action
parameters.description: The action writing or appending the helper invocation into startup files.

assertion_conditions: The action writes to shell startup configuration (profile directories or shell rc files).
The written content invokes a named helper (e.g., a script path) so it runs on subsequent shells.
The invocation is written in a failure-tolerant form that does not disturb the session.
exclusion_conditions: The action only creates the helper file without wiring it into startup configuration.
The startup file is edited for unrelated purposes (environment variables, aliases, PATH) with no helper invocation.
The invocation is written into a one-off command rather than persistent startup configuration.

new.name: REUSES_ARTIFACT_CREATED_BY_EARLIER_ACTION
new.definition: An artifact (file, credential, directory) produced by one action is consumed as an operational input by a later action, creating a traceable cross-action dependency on that produced value.

parameters.name: consumer_action
parameters.description: The later action whose command references the produced artifact.

parameters.name: producer_action
parameters.description: The earlier action that created the artifact.

assertion_conditions: The producer action creates a file, credential, or path at a specific location.
The consumer action's command references that same location as an input (e.g., a key path, a generated script path).
The producer precedes the consumer, and no other node supplies the artifact.
exclusion_conditions: Both actions merely reference an artifact that pre-existed and was not created by the producer.
The consumer action mentions the path only in narration without using it operationally.
The artifact was created by an action outside the compared pair.

new.name: CONFIRMS_DEPLOYMENT_PIPELINE
new.definition: A publishing action successfully writes content into the configured storage path, and a subsequent retrieval action reads that content back through the serving path, with the result showing the published content is being served.

parameters.name: publish_action
parameters.description: The action that commits/pushes/installs content into the repository or deployment source.

parameters.name: retrieval_action
parameters.description: The action that fetches the content through the serving endpoint.

parameters.name: served_result
parameters.description: The observation reporting the retrieved content and server response.

assertion_conditions: The publishing action reports success in writing the content to the deployment source.
The retrieval action addresses the serving endpoint that is supposed to expose that content after deployment.
The served result contains the published content with a success status, showing the publish-to-serve path works end to end.
exclusion_conditions: The retrieval occurs before the publishing action succeeds, so the served result cannot stem from that deployment.
The served content differs from what was published.
The retrieval reads a local copy or the repository directly rather than the serving endpoint.
